findings.evidence: On a pristine form with zero clinical severity, red carries three of the rubric's named non-severity meanings: a 'required' marker (asterisk on patient name), a destructive control (red × clearing the visit date), and validation blockers (red dot + red text chip in the summary deck, plus a red-tinted box under the study grid). The metric only caught the asterisk; the other three are plain to see in the screenshot.
findings.recommendation: Asterisk → --emr-text-secondary. Clear × → ghost muted icon (--emr-text-secondary, navy on hover). Remove the red-tinted box under the study grid and the red summary chip. The 'what's missing' state is a workflow state, so it lives once, as the existing neutral line next to the disabled CTA in the action bar (solid navy if it needs emphasis). Keep --emr-error for clinical severity on the study forms.

findings.evidence: Page background is white, the same as the card background (contrast 1.0). The four section decks are separated only by an outer hairline border, and only the summary deck carries a shadow. The metric passed on that 1-of-5 shadow, but visually the form decks are outlined boxes on white, not floating decks as in triage.png. This also breaks the Cards rule 'no outer border on primary content cards'.
findings.recommendation: Set the page field to the tinted --emr-bg-page / --emr-bg-accent-primary surface used by the references. Remove the outer border from all four section decks and give each --emr-shadow-card at radius --emr-border-radius-xl.

findings.evidence: All five decks shout the same way: a full-width gray header band, a full-height blue left rail (the rail treatment is reserved for alerts), an icon tile, a 'ნაბიჯი N' eyebrow and a bold title. The summary deck adds a gradient slab header. Step numbers appear twice, in the hero stepper and in every eyebrow. The stepper also reads '1/4 დასრულებულია' while showing step 1 as current and step 2 ticked, which breaks the single scan order.
findings.recommendation: Use the Section-headers rule: a slim row with a 4×15px --emr-gradient-primary tick and a --emr-font-md/600 title, a hairline under it, no tinted band, no left rail. Drop either the icon tiles or the 'ნაბიჯი N' eyebrows (the stepper already numbers the steps). Give the summary deck the same slim header instead of the gradient slab.

findings.evidence: On a triage screen meant to answer 'what do I do next', the decision that unlocks the only CTA (choosing studies, section 4) starts at about y≈1255, well below the 900px fold. findings.recommendation: Move the study picker up. findings.evidence: The metric's duplicateLabels (visit date, ICD-10) are subordinate mirrors in the summary deck (bothFullWeight:false). That is deliberate progressive disclosure and is allowed. The real repeats are the blocker messages: 'შეიყვანეთ პაციენტის სახელი' appears both in the summary chip and the action bar, and 'აირჩიეთ მინიმუმ ერთი კვლევა' appears in the summary and again in the louder red box.
findings.recommendation: Keep each blocker message only once, in the action bar next to the CTA. The summary deck should only mirror entered values.

reasoning: Light 1440 matches the metrics' colorScheme. The tier is triage, as given. The reference is triage.png, but the shape table would map this entry form to deep-dive.png, so confidence is 0.8. DESIGN-DIRECTION.md here has no 'Content & layout' section, so all findings trace to the Cards, Section-headers, Composition and Forms rules. The eye goes first to the two gradient slabs (hero, summary header) and then finds four identical banded, railed, numbered boxes on a white field. Nothing groups by depth and nothing ranks above anything else. Red shows up in four places with no clinical meaning at all. The one decision that matters, picking studies, is below the fold. Three dimensions score 1 or lower and colour discipline is 0, so the problem is the structure, not the tokens. Highest-leverage fix: tinted page field with borderless shadowed decks and slim tick headers, then lift the study picker above the fold and take red out of the required, clear and blocker roles.

findings.evidence: All four available study cards show a ✓ inside their selection circle while the red box below says no study is chosen ('დასაწყებად აირჩიეთ მინიმუმ ერთი კვლევა'). In light mode the same unselected state is an empty circle. Unselected and selected look the same, or reversed, in dark mode. The stepper has the same problem: step 2's completion tick is invisible white on white, steps 3 and 4 become solid blue dots that look done or active (outlined in light), and the moon icon in the theme toggle is invisible. Structure must not change with theme.
findings.recommendation: Unselected = empty circle with a hairline border in both themes. Checked = solid --emr-primary with a white ✓, as the Forms rule says. Stepper pending steps = outlined, completed = solid with a visible ✓, in both themes. Fix the dark tokens for the toggle icon and tick glyph so they contrast with their fill.

reasoning: Dark 1440 matches the metrics' colorScheme dark, and I compared it against triage-dark.png. Elevation is fine here (1.22, decks visible), so the light-mode elevation failure doesn't carry over. Composition is the same as light: equal-weight banded decks and the study picker below the fold. Dark mode adds a state-legibility failure, P1 on an intake that selects which studies get done: every available study looks ticked while the warning says none is selected, and the stepper's done and pending states are reversed or invisible. Highest-leverage fix: make the checked, unchecked and stepper states identical in both themes, then apply the light-mode structural fixes.
